canonical_title: Google to acquire de-identified Spirit Airlines business data for AI training
aliases: Spirit Airlines AI training data sale
treatment: Treat Google's $10M agreement to buy de-identified Spirit Airlines internal business data for product development and AI-model training as covered. Reinclude only for court approval/rejection, material changes to dataset scope or privacy terms, disclosure of model/training use, or similar large enterprise-data acquisitions that materially change interpretation.
known_facts: Reuters reported Google agreed to pay $10 million for internal business data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines for product development and training its AI models.
The dataset includes employee emails, Microsoft Teams messages, spreadsheets, calendars, and marketing, productivity, and operations data.
The data is to be de-identified before the sale closes and is described as containing no customer information or personally identifiable information.
A U.S. bankruptcy judge is scheduled to consider approval of the sale at a Wednesday hearing.
AI data company Mercor submitted a competing $7.5 million bid.
reinclude_only_if: The bankruptcy court approves, rejects, or materially changes the sale.
Google discloses which models, products, or training objectives use the dataset.
Material privacy, labor, copyright, or data-governance restrictions are imposed.
Google makes another comparable acquisition that establishes a broader enterprise-training-data strategy.
notes: NEW in 2026-08-18 Midday. The sale still requires bankruptcy-court consideration; do not describe it as fully closed until approved and completed.
